extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, KIPO examiners, and IP practitioners dealing with Korean patent procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and criteria for formalities examination, return/invalidation of application documents, amendment and revocation procedures, interruption/suspension/resumption of patent-related proceedings under the Enforcement Rules of the Korean Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return of illegitimate application documents (Article 11 general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent application or related document falls under any of the listed subparagraphs, the Commissioner of KIPO or the President of the IP Trial & Appeal Board shall not deem such application documents to be legitimate (except for special provisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If documents are illegitimate the Commissioner/President shall deliver notice of intention to return, grounds for return, and a period for explanation; in some cases documents must be returned immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: Violation of format/preparation requirements (Article 11(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Article 2 of the Enforcement Rules of the Patent Act is violated and a document is not prepared per an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical formal defect; falls within the list of grounds for deeming documents illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: Unclear type of application or document (Article 11(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the type of an application or a document is not clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents whose nature cannot be determined may be treated as illegitimate and returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: Missing or unclear applicant identity (Article 11(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the name (title for a juristic person) or the applicant code of the person who conducts the patent-related proceeding (or in absence of code the name and address) is not indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifying information must be present; omission renders the document illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: Non-Korean language filing (Article 11(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application is not written in Korean.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must be in Korean unless otherwise permitted; absence of Korean text is ground for non-acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: Missing specification/description (Article 11(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a specification is not attached to an application (including where the description of the invention is not included in the specification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application without a specification/description is illegitimate and may be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: Specification attached lacks claims and amendment period elapsed (Article 11(5-2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a specification which does not include the claims is attached to a patent application filed by the lawful holder of a right and the amendment period under Article 42(2)(ii) has already elapsed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late submission of claims after specified amendment period is not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: Applicant lacks Korean domicile or business (Article 11(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application document was submitted by a person who has neither a domicile nor a place of business in the Republic of Korea, other than a patent administrator under Article 5(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign submitters must be authorized/represented as required; otherwise documents may be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: Documents not submitted within designated period (Article 11(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the documents were not submitted within the designated period under the Patent Act or any order under the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late filings beyond allowable periods are grounds for return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: Period-extension request not allowable (Article 11(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for extension of the period was submitted for the period not allowed for extension among the periods stipulated under the Patent Act or any order under the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to extend non-extendable periods are illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: Extension request filed after allowable period (Article 11(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for extension of the period was submitted after the expiration of the period for requesting a trial under Article 132(17) or the period designated by the Commissioner/President/an administrative patent judge or an examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late extension requests after expiration are not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: Documents submitted after termination of proceeding (Article 11(10))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where documents regarding a patent-related proceeding have been submitted after the termination of such patent-related proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions after termination are illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: Unauthorized person submitted documents (Article 11(11))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person not entitled to carry out a patent-related proceeding has submitted documents regarding the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only authorized persons or representatives may validly submit documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: Required annexed forms/documents unclear (Article 11(12))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where documents such as the report in Annexed Form No.2 (restriction of reliance on general power of attorney), application for registration of general power of attorney in Form No.3, application for change/withdrawal of registration, application for grant of applicant code in Form No.4, etc., are not clear and cannot be accepted when an application code should be granted based on them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific annexed forms must be clear and complete for applicant code grant or related actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: Electronic submission/format defects (Article 11(13))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent application or any document submitted over a computerized network or via electronic recording device is not prepared by using the software offered by KIPO or where electronic documents are submitted in a condition where they cannot be handled in the electronic data processing system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic filings must conform to KIPO software/format requirements or they may be rejected/returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: Failure to submit documents required under Article 3(2)(ii) within designated period (Article 11(13-2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where documents required to be submitted under Article 3(2)(ii) have not been submitted within the designated period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submission of specifically required documents is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: Failure to submit documents required under Article 8 within allowed explanation period (Article 11(14))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where documents required to be submitted under Article 8 have not been submitted within the period allowed for explanation without any legitimate explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no legitimate reason is given, missing documents under Article 8 are ground for return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: Request for examination attached to specification lacking claims (Article 11(15))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent applicant has submitted a request for examination on a patent application attached with a specification which does not include the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for examination must be accompanied by claims; absence renders request illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: Request for early publication without claims (Article 11(16))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for early publication has been submitted for a patent application attached with a description which does not include claims or a patent registered for publication under Article 87(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early publication requests require claims to be present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: Decision to grant cannot be delayed (Article 11(17))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a decision to grant a patent cannot be delayed since the application falls under sub-subparagraphs of Article 40(2)(i) of the Enforcement Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some statutory situations require immediate processing and may make other submissions illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: Examination cannot be deferred (Article 11(18))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examination on a patent application cannot be deferred since the application falls under sub-subparagraphs of Article 40(3)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory non-deferable examinations must be processed accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: Request for re-examination without amendment or otherwise barred (Article 11(19))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for re-examination without amendment of a specification or drawing(s) attached to a patent application has been made or where a request for re-examination cannot be made since the application falls under Article 67(2)(i) of the Enforcement Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-examination requests must comply with amendment and eligibility rules; otherwise they are illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: Missing Korean translation subject to other Articles (Article 11(20))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Korean translation is not yet submitted or where it is subject to Article 53(1)(ii), Article 59(2)(ii) or Article 64(2)(ii) of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide required Korean translations within applicable provisions is a ground for return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examination definition and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A formalities examination is a review procedure conducted by the Commissioner of KIPO or the President of the IP Trial & Appeal Board regarding a patent-related proceeding under Article 46 of the Patent Act and Article 11 of the Enforcement Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If irregularities are found the commissioner/president shall order amendment, invalidate the proceeding, or return documents after giving applicant an opportunity to explain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who conducts formalities examinations and transfer rules
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle formalities examinations are conducted by divisions in charge (Application Division, International Application Division, Registration Division or Trial Policy Division) under the name of the Commissioner/President; however, where irregularities are closely linked to substantive examinations the formalities examination shall be conducted by an examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner finds formalities issues closely linked to substantive matters they describe irregularities and transfer to the divisions; divisions then complete formalities exam and re-transfer to examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for amendment prior to invalidation (invalidation procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent-related proceeding falls under any subparagraph of Article 46, an examiner shall request an amendment in the name of the Commissioner. The request shall state bibliographic data, amendment period, documents to be amended and written amendments in detail, including specific contents violating procedural requirements and amendment methods if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment period designated in a request for amendment shall be within one month.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of timely amendment on invalidation (acceptance of amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where irregularities have been addressed through submission of an amendment within the designated period, the application shall be deemed amended and not invalidated; if amendment is not submitted or irregularities not addressed, examiner can invalidate the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments cure defects if timely and responsive to requested items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments submitted after designated period but before date of invalidation (Article 3①)
rubrics_metrics.description: If amendment is submitted after expiration of the designated period but before delivery date of notice of invalidation, examiner shall not invalidate the application and shall accept the amendment. An amendment submitted after the date of invalidation shall be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If amendment mailed before date of invalidation but overlooked, examiner shall revoke invalidation and accept amendment; same treatment for amendment submitted on date of invalidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: New irregularities discovered after amendment (fees and further amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: When new irregularities are found after an amendment is completed, an examiner shall set a period and request amendment again; applicant shall pay amendment fees for each amendment. However, if items omitted in first amendment are ordered to be amended again, additional fees for those items shall not be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Instruction on Payment of amendment fee; fees may be required per separate amendment except for certain omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary amendment including irrelevant items (acceptance and fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a voluntary amendment irrelevant to the amendment request is submitted while a written amendment by the request for amendment has not been submitted, an examiner shall accept the amendment. If the amended items fall under items for which amendment fees are paid, the amendment fee shall be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voluntary broader amendments are accepted but may incur fees for particular amended items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial amendment when multiple items requested (partial invalidation and separate fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: If examiner requests amendment to more than two proceedings in a single request and amendment contains only parts of the proceedings, examiner shall invalidate only the proceedings whose irregularities are not addressed. If more than two items required for amendment have been amended in two or more separate amendments, it shall be deemed separate amendments and fees for separate amendments shall be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial compliance leads to partial invalidation; separate amendments treated separately for fee purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of only amended items without formal amendment procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Where only the amended items are submitted without using the formalities of an amendment, examiner shall accept the document first and then request amendment to the amendment proceeding citing violation of amendment formalities. If type of document unclear, return it. If irregularities are minor, examiner can accept without requesting amendment. If formalities violation not corrected within period, examiner shall invalidate the amendment proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor formal defects may be overlooked; persistent noncompliance leads to invalidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to invalidate proceedings (who may invalidate)
rubrics_metrics.description: The person who can invalidate a patent-related proceeding is the Commissioner of KIPO or the President of the IP Trial & Appeal Board, not an examiner. Subjects of invalidation are not limited to application proceedings; all patent-related proceedings may be invalidated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When examiner intends to invalidate they must state grounds and notify the person who conducted the proceeding; notice must attach information that applicant can conduct administrative trial or lawsuit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation for unpaid examination fees due to claim increase after third-party amendment (additional fee rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where additional payment of examination fees is required since the number of claims increased because of amendments to the description after a request for examination made by a person other than the applicant, but the applicant has not paid the examination fees, an examiner shall invalidate the amendment proceeding for a description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must pay additional fees if claim count increases caused by third-party-initiated amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of invalidation (deemed never filed and priority effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is invalidated, the application is deemed to have never been filed for purposes of Articles 36(1)–(3). An application claiming domestic priority cannot be filed based on inventions disclosed in the description or drawings originally attached to the concerned application. The right to request compensation is deemed never to have existed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invalidation has severe retroactive effects on filing and priority rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation of invalidation for unavoidable causes (two-month request; one-year limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where invalidation occurred but failure to amend within the designated period is recognized to have been caused by reasons not attributable to the person ordered to amend, the Commissioner can revoke the invalidation if a request is made within two months of the day when such unavoidable causes are extinguished. However, when one year has elapsed after the designated period expires, revocation is not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unavoidable causes include natural disasters and other reasons an ordinary person cannot avoid; unawareness of service is not included absent special reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for requesting revocation of invalidation (evidence and form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant seeking revocation must attach a copy of evidential document for reasons of laches to a written request in Annexed Form No.10; if legal representative is present, attach power of representation evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow required form and attach supporting evidence to substantiate unavoidable cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision on revocation and effect on amendment period
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether to revoke invalidation shall be determined by the examiner (or division) that invalidated the application; examiner/division shall notify the requester and state that amendment can be made within the period corresponding to the original amendment period from time of revocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocation restores the opportunity to amend within analogous time as originally allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of proceedings conducted between invalidation and revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent-related proceeding or examination is conducted during the period after invalidation and before revocation, an examiner shall review the proceeding or examination and determine whether such proceeding or examination takes effect by considering the effect made by the revocation of invalidation and the confidence protection principle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effects of interim proceedings depend on final revocation decision and protection of legitimate expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and immediate return procedures for return of documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner/President shall deliver notification stating intention to return application documents, ground for rejection and the period for explanation. If applicant requests return, Commissioner/President shall return documents immediately. If applicant fails to submit explanation or request for return within period, or explanation is groundless, documents shall be returned immediately after expiration of period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must include information about administrative trial or lawsuit rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's response to notice of grounds for rejection (explanation vs amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant can submit an explanation or opinion on the notice of grounds for rejection within the period for explanation; however, the applicant is not allowed to submit an amendment in order to address the grounds for rejection of application documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matters to be amended in proceedings include formal irregularities; substantive issues (e.g., foreigner capacity or patentability) are not to be immediately rejected but accepted first for substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent completion of proceeding when failure due to causes not attributable
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person failed to comply with the period for requesting a trial or retrial because of a cause not attributable to the person, they may subsequently complete the proceeding within the designated period; period allowed is within 2 months of the day when the cause ceases, and one year limit applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects parties disadvantaged by unavoidable causes; one-year absolute bar applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of patent application (request for examination/reexamination after unavoidable cause)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant fails to comply with certain periods due to reasons unattributable to them causing revocation or confirmation of rejection, applicant may file a request for examination or reexamination within two months from the date such grounds cease to exist; but if one year has passed from expiration date of the concerned period, no request may be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to specific periods (e.g., periods under Article 59(2)/(3) and Article 67(2)(i)); Notwithstanding Article 59(5), timely request deems application not withdrawn or decision not final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Succession and continuation of proceedings on transfer (Article 18–19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effects of a proceeding extend to the successor to the patent or patent-related right. Where a patent or right is transferred while a proceeding is pending, the Commissioner or presiding judge may permit the successor to continue the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural effects transfer with ownership; successor may carry on pending matters subject to permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interruption of proceeding — statutory causes (Article 20 list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceeding shall be interrupted in cases such as: 1) relevant party dies; 2) corporate party dissolves in course of merger; 3) relevant party loses capacity to perform; 4) party's legal representative dies or loses power; 5) duty of party as trustee terminates; 6) representative appointed under proviso to Article 11(1) dies or disqualified; 7) bankruptcy trustee or intervening person becomes disqualified or dies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interruption is due to legal reasons and generally requires a legitimate successor to resume the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resumption of interrupted proceeding — who may resume (Article 21 list)
rubrics_metrics.description: If proceeding interrupted under Article 20, persons who may resume include: 1) deceased party's heir, administrator of inherited property, or authorized person (subject to renunciation period); 2) corporation established or surviving after merger; 3) reinstated party or appointed legal representative; 4) new trustee; 5) new representative or either party; 6) equally qualified person when trustee/intervener disqualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resumption is limited to legitimate successors or authorized persons as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for resumption procedures and notifications (Article 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for resuming an interrupted proceeding can be filed by persons specified in Article 21; upon receipt the Commissioner or presiding judge shall notify the opposite party. The Commissioner/judge may examine ex officio and dismiss if no grounds to accept. If resumption request follows service of certified copy of decision/ruling, Commissioner/judge determines whether to permit resumption. If specified person fails to resume, Commissioner/judge may order them to resume within a specified period; if not resumed, it is deemed resumed on the day following expiration and all parties are notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposing parties may request ordering of resumption; administrative oversight ensures resumption or deemed resumption with notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of proceeding — causes and revocation (Article 23)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Commissioner or administrative patent judge is unable to perform duties due to natural disaster or extenuating circumstances, proceeding shall be suspended until circumstances cease. If relevant party is unable to resume due to an obstacle persisting for indefinite duration, Commissioner/judge may order suspension until obstacle removed. Commissioner/judge may revoke such determination and must notify relevant parties when suspending or revoking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension protects proceedings during institutional incapacity or prolonged obstacles; formal notifications required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of interruption or suspension on running periods (Article 24)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent-related proceeding is interrupted or suspended, the running of the relevant period shall be interrupted, and the entire period shall start to run again from the time the resumption is notified or the proceeding is resumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timelines pause during interruption/suspension and restart upon resumption/notification; parties regain full period thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Discontinuation vs interruption vs suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Discontinuation of a patent-related proceeding refers to a condition where the proceeding does not legally proceed before completion. The Patent Act divides discontinuation into interruption (when cause attributable to party prevents proceeding until successor shows up) and suspension (when cause prevents KIPO or party from conducting proceeding and suspension is legal or by KIPO decision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding difference is important for rights to resume, timelines, and remedies.
